title: Garlic: modeled ₹3,703/qtl left, Solan → Dharamshala
summary: January 2025: reported garlic prices at Solan and Dharamshala imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 97% of 31 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹3,703 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 192 same-variety market pairs screened for garlic in January 2025; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Dharamshala report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: January 2025
scenes.caption: Solan (Himachal Pradesh) and Dharamshala (Himachal Pradesh) both reported garlic prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 31 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Solan reported a median ₹23,250 per quintal. Dharamshala reported a median ₹29,000 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹6,000/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹6,000 per quintal, and Dharamshala was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 269 km by road
scenes.caption: 269 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~4 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹58/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹3,269 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹1,794 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Dharamshala report, the rule selects 31 of 31 modeled shipping days. 30 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹3,703 per quintal (₹2,204 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Garlic route from Solan to Dharamshala was positive on 97% of matched days in January 2025. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹370,300, or ₹220,400 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to garlic
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹58/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Garlic route from Solan to Dharamshala was positive on 97% of matched days in January 2025. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹370,300, or ₹220,400 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

conclusion: The modeled Garlic route from Ganaur to Kangra (Baijnath) was positive on 100% of matched days in September 2025. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹205,100, or ₹148,100 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.
